title.title: Exact derandomization of logarithmic space
title.subtitle: Claim: $\mathsf L = \mathsf{RL} = \mathsf{BPL}$, coin flips never help log-space machines with bounded error

plain: Does a computer with tiny memory ever need to flip coins? The claim: no, coin tosses never help it

beats.text: A machine with $O(\log n)$ memory that may flip coins: how much space to remove them?
Since Saks–Zhou in 1999 the answer sat at $\log^{3/2} n$, with Hoza shaving a bit in 2021
The claim: plain $\log n$ suffices, the space twin of P = BPP

steps: Estimate the chance of acceptance level by level
Most random seeds give an accurate estimate
Seeds are short: try every one and take the middle answer
